title: Guarding the Tongue
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Guarding the tongue means bringing speech under the lordship of Christ. Words can heal or destroy, so believers must reject gossip, slander, lying, harshness, flattery, manipulation, and careless speech.
summary: Guarding the tongue means bringing speech under the lordship of Christ. Words can heal or destroy, so believers must reject gossip, slander, lying, harshness, flattery, manipulation, and careless speech.
christFocus: Jesus Christ spoke with perfect truth, purity, authority, and grace. His people are called to let their words reflect His character and build others up according to truth.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture warns that the tongue is powerful. Words can bless or curse, heal or wound, build up or tear down. Speech reveals the condition of the heart.

Guarding the tongue requires more than avoiding obvious lies. Believers must resist gossip, slander, bitterness, manipulation, filthy talk, harsh correction, exaggeration, and careless promises.

God’s Word calls speech to be gracious and useful for building others up. Words should fit the need, give grace to hearers, and honor the Lord.

Jesus warns that people will give account for their words. Speech is not small before God. The mouth must be brought under the rule of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many relationships are deeply wounded by words spoken in anger, pride, sarcasm, or secrecy. Guarding the tongue protects souls, families, churches, and friendships.

This doctrine also confronts spiritual hypocrisy. A person cannot bless God while freely using words to destroy people made in His image.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to rule your mouth. Before speaking, posting, correcting, joking, or repeating information, consider whether your words honor Christ and help others. Confess sinful speech quickly, seek forgiveness where needed, and practice words that give grace.
